cedre_protocol_points_used.water_sorption: water retention is measured by weighing water-saturated sorbent
cedre_protocol_points_used.protocol_1: low agitation for 20 min followed by 30 min draining
cedre_protocol_points_used.protocol_2_optional: 15 min and optionally 24 h contact, followed by 30 s draining
cedre_protocol_points_used.boom_class: pillows, socks or booms = type D/E
cedre_protocol_points_used.hydrophobicity_definition: retention capacity of water / retention capacity of oil

cedre_compatible_internal_go_no_go.scope: internal pre-screen for boom-like D/E candidate before requesting external Cedre testing

oil_uptake_g_g.status_note: Internal operationalization of Cedre's D/E sorption-capacity-in-weight criterion >10; do not quote g/g as a verbatim unit from the supplied Cedre sheet unless later documentation explicitly states the unit.

water_to_oil_retention_ratio.origin: Cedre hydrophobicity criterion for floating sorbents

retrievable_envelope.origin: JANUS/SCOBY-D0 project-specific containment requirement; not presented as a Cedre criterion

cedre_compatible_internal_go_no_go.decision: PASS only if all listed pre-screen criteria pass; otherwise NO_GO_FOR_EXTERNAL_BOOM_TEST_REQUEST

relationship_to_existing_M1_gates.M1_G1_UPTAKE: existing internal median surrogate-oil uptake >=10 g/g in artificial seawater remains unchanged
relationship_to_existing_M1_gates.M1_G2_SELECTIVITY: existing internal oil/water uptake ratio >=5 remains unchanged; if definitions align exactly, this corresponds to water/oil <=0.20 and is stricter than Cedre's <0.25 floor
relationship_to_existing_M1_gates.M1_G4_RETRIEVAL: existing >=99% dry-equivalent retrieval and no hazardous fragmentation remains unchanged
relationship_to_existing_M1_gates.M1_G5_PRESS_RECOVERY: existing >=60% single-press recovery remains an internal project target when closed-loop recovery is claimed
relationship_to_existing_M1_gates.M1_G6_to_G8: salinity, dynamic robustness and independent-batch replication remain mandatory internal gates

notes: Live/raw fermentation material is outside the intended marine deployment candidate class.
Only purified, neutral, contained/retrievable BC architectures may advance to environmental testing.
Any hydrophobic treatment remains blocked from environmental-safety claims until leachate/ecotoxicity evidence exists.
Passing this pre-screen does not authorize open-water or petroleum deployment.
